coverage_quote: The ISC-GEM Global Instrumental Earthquake Catalogue (1904-2021) was prepared by a team of international experts... extended on a yearly basis as new data becomes available.
completeness_quote: The cut-off magnitudes for earthquakes to be included in the catalogue are Ms >= 7.5 (1904-1917), Ms >= 6.25 (1918-1959), and Ms >= 5.5 (1960 onwards). Global completeness Mc is approximately 5.6-6.4.
notes: Verified directly against ISC-GEM web documentation and FDSN web service. Provides globally uniform Mw with rigorously derived uncertainties.

span: 1964-01-01 to present (24-month review delay; preliminary to present)
magnitude_type: Mixed (mb; Ms; ML; Mw with ISC prime hypocentres)
completeness: M >= 4.5 globally (1964+); M >= 3.5 in dense regional subnets
licence: Free for academic/research use with attribution
licence_quote: Data from the ISC is free for academic and research use. The user must acknowledge the ISC as the source of the data and cite the primary ISC papers.
coverage_quote: The definitive ISC Reviewed Bulletin is available from 1964 to 24 months before the current date; preliminary data are available up to the present.
completeness_quote: The ISC Bulletin is complete down to approximately M 4.5 globally from 1964, and lower in regions of dense station coverage.
notes: Verified via FDSN web service endpoint. Standard definitive source for global phase readings and prime hypocentres.

magnitude_type: Mw (derived directly from inverted seismic moment tensor M0)
licence: Public Domain / Open Scientific Data (NSF supported; citation required)
licence_quote: The Global CMT catalog is open scientific data supported by the National Science Foundation. Use of these data should reference Dziewonski, Chou and Woodhouse (1981) and Ekstrom, Nettles and Dziewonski (2012).
coverage_quote: The project maintains a catalog of moment tensors starting in 1976 and continuing through the present day with minimal delay.
completeness_quote: The standard CMT project produces centroid-moment tensors for earthquakes with Mw >= 5.5 globally from 1976 to the present, and Mw >= 5.0 in the modern era.
notes: Verified via live CGI query. Gold standard for focal mechanisms and independent Mw.

provider: Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES) Government of India
licence_quote: National Center for Seismology data is governed by the Government Open Data License - India (GODL). Free commercial and non-commercial use with attribution to Ministry of Earth Sciences.
coverage_quote: Historical seismicity dating back to 1505 AD and modern instrumental observations from the National Seismological Network.
completeness_quote: The network provides earthquake parameters within 5-10 minutes. Threshold of detection is M >= 3.0 in Peninsular India and M >= 3.5 to 4.0 in the Himalayan belt.
notes: Primary national agency for seismic monitoring in India. Portal verified operational.

provider: National Earthquake Monitoring and Research Center (NEMRC) / Department of Mines and Geology (DMG) Nepal
magnitude_type: ML (local magnitude calibrated by DMG/DASE for Nepal)
licence: Public Government Seismic Record (free for research with attribution)
licence_quote: Official government earthquake bulletins produced by the Department of Mines and Geology, Government of Nepal. Available for scientific research and public information with citation.
coverage_quote: Continuous seismic monitoring of the Nepal Himalaya since 1994 established in collaboration with DASE (France).
completeness_quote: The National Earthquake Monitoring and Research Center records seismic events across Nepal. Complete for ML >= 4.0 throughout Nepal and ML >= 2.0 in the central network.
notes: Verified against live HTML bulletin at seismonepal.gov.np. Essential for local ML calibration and aftershock tracking.

provider: China Earthquake Administration (CEA) / National Earthquake Data Center (NEDC)
magnitude_type: Ms (surface wave magnitude; Chinese national standard GB 17740-1999); ML; mb
licence: China Public Science & Technology Data Policy (free research use with citation)
licence_quote: China Earthquake Administration National Earthquake Data Center Scientific Data Sharing Policy. Free for scientific research with mandatory citation of the CENC catalog.
coverage_quote: Formal catalogue spanning 1970 to present with real-time and reviewed bulletins.
completeness_quote: Formal earthquake catalog of China Earthquake Networks Center. Complete down to Ms >= 3.0 in eastern China and Ms >= 4.0 in western China (Qinghai-Tibet plateau).
notes: Verified via CEIC real-time and reviewed earthquake distribution portals. Primary reference for Tibetan Plateau seismicity.

provider: Roger Bilham (2019) / Nicholas Ambraseys & James Jackson (2003)
magnitude_type: Mw (inferred moment magnitude from macroseismic intensities and paleoseismology)
completeness: Incomplete; M >= 7.5 major events recorded with substantial spatiotemporal uncertainties
licence: Academic Fair Use / Scholarly Review (Geological Society / Current Science)
licence_quote: Scholarly review published in Geological Society Special Publications and Current Science (Indian Academy of Sciences). Open for scholarly citation and research redistribution.
coverage_quote: Covers documented historical earthquakes from 1100 AD to the late 19th century along the Himalayan arc.
completeness_quote: Severely incomplete prior to 1800; only mega-events (Mw >= 7.5-8.0) such as 1255, 1505, 1555, 1803, and 1833 leave surviving records.
notes: Verified against Ambraseys & Jackson (2003) Current Science and Bilham (2019) GSL Spec Pub 483.

completeness_quote: Demonstrated global completeness for Mw >= 7.0 from 1900 to present across all subduction and continental collision zones.
